overall.summary: The observed protective association of GLP-1 agonists with breast cancer (matched OR 0.695, 95% CI 0.590–0.819) is compromised by severe confounding and selection bias. Women with prior breast cancer were not excluded and were substantially more prevalent in the control group (7.8% vs 5.9% in the matched cohort; 9.2% vs 5.9% overall). Combined with an exposure definition requiring no minimum duration or cumulative dose, non-exclusion of prevalent cases, and lack of time-to-event analysis over a short 3.5-year window, the estimated risk reduction is driven by methodological artifacts rather than a true biological protective effect.
